      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      properties:

          title: Title
          description: >-
            The optional honorific title of the pet owner (for example MR, MRS,
            MS or DR). When present it is used to compose the 'salutation'.
          type: string
          maxLength: 10
          example: MR
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string

          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"

        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: >-
            The postal address of the pet owner. Accepted on input for backward
            compatibility with the flat address form; when the structured
            'addressLine1' is supplied it is preferred and this value is ignored.
            On output this is the composed, normalized address: the normalized
            'addressLine1', with a single space and the normalized 'addressLine2'
            appended when 'addressLine2' is present.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          pattern: '.*\S.*'
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        addressLine1:
          title: Address line 1
          description: >-
            The first line of the structured postal address of the pet owner.
            Preferred over the flat 'address' when present. An owner is valid
            when it supplies an address in EITHER form (a non-blank
            'addressLine1', or the flat 'address'). Normalized on create
            (upper-cased, whitespace collapsed, common street-type
            abbreviations expanded).
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          pattern: '.*\S.*'
          example: '10 King St'
        addressLine2:
          title: Address line 2
          description: >-
            The optional second line of the structured postal address of the pet
            owner (for example a unit or apartment number). Normalized on create
            like 'addressLine1' and, when present, appended to the composed
            'address' after a single space.
          type: string
          maxLength: 255
          example: 'Unit 5'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          pattern: '.*\S.*'
          example: Madison
        postcode:
          title: Postcode
          description: >-
            The 4-digit postcode of the pet owner. Optional; when present it
            must be four digits and, when the owner's city has a known region
            (Sydney->NSW, Melbourne->VIC, Brisbane->QLD), must fall within that
            region's range (NSW 2000-2099, VIC 3000-3099, QLD 4000-4099). A city
            with no known region accepts any 4-digit postcode. Stored and
            returned when given.
          type: string
          pattern: '^[0-9]{4}$'
          example: '2000'
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: >-
            The telephone number of the pet owner. On create the value is
            normalized to E.164 form: spaces, dashes and brackets are stripped;
            a leading '+' and country code are kept when present, otherwise the
            country code '+61' is assumed and a single leading '0' is dropped
            from the national digits. The result must be a '+' followed by 8 to
            15 digits. For example '0412 345 678' is stored as '+61412345678'.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          example: '+61412345678'
        email:
          title: Email address
          description: >-
            The email address of the pet owner. Optional; when present it must
            be a syntactically valid address and is stored and returned
            lower-cased.
          type: string
          format: email
          maxLength: 255
          example: george.franklin@example.com
        registrationDate:
          title: Registration date
          description: >-
            The date the pet owner was registered, in ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD' format.

            date.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '2026-08-11'
        birthDate:
          title: Birth date

            registrationDate. Stored and returned when given.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '1990-01-01'

            with an existing owner. When true, the duplicate-household check
            (same last name and address) is bypassed. Optional; defaults to
            false and is not stored.
          type: boolean
          writeOnly: true
          default: false
          example: false

            initials:

              description: >-

                names, dot-separated with a trailing dot.
              type: string
              example: 'G.F.'
              readOnly: true
            telephoneDisplay:
              title: Telephone display
              description: >-

                country code, a space, then the national digits grouped in
                threes from the left and separated by spaces. The raw

                fiscal year of the business-day-adjusted registrationDate, the
                first 8 upper-case hex characters of the SHA-256 digest of the
                normalized telephone concatenated with the last name, and a
                single Luhn check digit (CHK) computed over the digits of
                '<REGION><FY><HASH8>'.
              type: string
              example: 'NSW261A2B3C4D7'

                every owner in that household carries the same value.
              type: string

              readOnly: true

              description: >-

              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 1
              readOnly: true
            fiscalYear:
              title: Fiscal year
              description: >-

                year starts on 1 July.
              type: string
              example: 'FY26'
              readOnly: true
            membershipPoints:
              title: Membership points
              description: >-
                The owner's membership points, assigned at creation. Points

                the owner has no namesakes (namesakeCount is 0), 2 for a

              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 5
              readOnly: true
            membershipLevel:
              title: Membership level
              description: >-

              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 1
              maximum: 4
              example: 3
              readOnly: true

              description: >-

              description: >-

                using the fixed table (NSW->Australia/Sydney,

                the region is not in the table.
              type: string
              example: 'Australia/Sydney'
              readOnly: true
            ownerSegment:

              description: >-

                'PREMIUM' when membershipLevel is 3 or more, otherwise
                'STANDARD'. AREA is 'METRO' when the locality is a known region
                (NSW, VIC or QLD), otherwise 'REGIONAL'.

              enum:

              readOnly: true
            ageBand:

            bulkSignupWarning:

I implemented the `riskFlag` rule for the `POST /api/owners` → `GET /api/owners/{id}` endpoint. The flag is `true` when any of the three conditions hold, otherwise `false`:

1. **Possible duplicate** — the owner's stored `possibleDuplicate` is true (already computed at creation via the soundex-lastName + postcode soft-match).

- **`OwnerMapper.java`** — added a `@Mapping` expression deriving `riskFlag` from the owner, consistent with the other derived fields.

Note: since the concept isn't stored on the entity, I derived `riskFlag` at mapping time from existing stored fields (`possibleDuplicate`, `capacityWarning`) plus the email — no schema/DB migration needed. The one thing I had to interpret was "disposable-adjacent" (the spec text in the test Javadoc was truncated); I read it as the provider-label match described above, which is the natural fit given exact disposable domains are already rejected before an owner can be fetched.
